body.q: A family from Manchester travels to Spain for a two-week holiday. Which type of tourism is this?
body.why: Outbound tourism is when residents of a country travel to another country, so from the UK perspective a trip to Spain is outbound.

body.q: A tourist from Japan visits Kenya on a safari holiday. From Kenya's perspective, which type of tourism is this?
body.why: Inbound tourism describes visitors arriving in a country from another country, so Kenya receives an inbound tourist.

body.q: A couple from Sydney spends a long weekend in the Blue Mountains, also in Australia. Which type of tourism does this describe?
body.why: Domestic tourism is when people travel within their own country.

o: Attending an international trade fair in Dubai
Taking a cruise around the Caribbean
Going on a skiing holiday in Switzerland
body.q: Which of the following is an example of business tourism?
body.why: Business tourism involves travel for work-related purposes such as conferences, meetings, exhibitions and trade fairs.

body.q: A group of friends travels to Rio de Janeiro to experience Carnival. Which type of tourism does this best describe?
body.why: Cultural tourism involves travelling to experience a destination's festivals, traditions, heritage and way of life.

body.q: A traveller goes to Thailand for a dental procedure that costs less than at home and combines it with a few days on the beach. Which type of tourism is the main reason for this trip?
body.why: Medical tourism is travelling abroad to receive medical or dental treatment, often for lower cost or shorter waiting times.

o: Wanting to escape a stressful daily routine
A famous landmark in another country
body.q: Which of the following is a 'push' factor that might motivate someone to travel on holiday?
body.why: Push factors are personal motivations within the traveller, such as the need to relax, whereas the other options are features of destinations that pull visitors.

o: A warm climate and sandy beaches
A tourist feeling tired of work
A person needing a break from study
A family wanting to spend time together
body.q: Which of the following is the best example of a 'pull' factor for a destination?
body.why: Pull factors are attractions or qualities of a destination, such as climate and scenery, that draw tourists to it.

body.q: A person travels to a different city for the weekend specifically to attend their cousin's wedding. Which reason for travel is this?
body.why: Travel to attend family events or see relatives is classified as visiting friends and relatives (VFR).

body.q: A tour operator offers trips to a rainforest where small groups stay in locally owned lodges, and part of the fee supports wildlife conservation. Which type of tourism is this?
body.why: Eco-tourism involves responsible travel to natural areas that protects the environment and benefits local communities.

topic: Types of tourism & reasons to travel
